issues_outside_coverage: Dependency exemption deduction under sec. 151(c) for BB (2015 and 2016) disallowed
2016: petitioner allowed an education credit for spring 2016 tuition paid with Federal direct student loan proceeds credited in 2016 (amount not stated; computation left to Rule 155)
Timing of payment of qualified tuition under sec. 1.25A-5(e)(3) (loan proceeds treated as paid when credited); prepayment rule of sec. 25A(g)(4) not relevant
Effect of State court order (Journal Entry of Support) allocating the dependency exemption: not binding for Federal tax purposes after 1984
decisive_judgment_findings: BB spent more than one-half of his nights in 2015 and 2016 with his mother; petitioner's testimony that BB's residence was his apartment was self-serving and uncorroborated (no log, calendar or journal)
BB's mother had sole legal custody and was the custodial parent; petitioner was the noncustodial parent
No Form 8332 or equivalent written declaration from BB's mother was obtained or attached for 2015 or 2016; the mother claimed BB on her own returns
Petitioner's AGI exceeded the no-qualifying-child EIC limit for both years ($14,820 for 2015; $14,880 for 2016)
Fall 2015 tuition was fully paid by a Pell grant, so no qualified tuition was paid by petitioner in 2015
Spring 2016 tuition was paid partly with Federal direct loan proceeds credited to petitioner's account in 2016, so petitioner paid qualified expenses in 2016

2016 (docket 10104-18): decision under Rule 155 with no final deficiency figure stated; no 2016 deficiency value recorded in this key (notice deficiency was $4,673, reduced by the allowed 2016 education credit)
